title: New order with freedom to choose comfort

captions.physics: Changing routines in response to understanding
captions.energy: Making new rules fixed and compulsory

meaning: Your domestic support preserves freedom when new understanding allows familiar convenience to be discussed instead of turning change into compulsory loss of everything familiar.
text: New understanding of domestic life may encourage different action while preserving what matters to both. Judgement in the physical position of Muladhara appears through this changed participation. The Emperor in energy can make new rules immovable, while the Devil in emotions holds to familiar comfort. Renewal can meet resistance for reasons beyond its meaning: rigid form requires immediate loss of pleasure without room to discuss cost. Both struggle to choose between necessary change and familiar convenience that still matters greatly.

For example, you realise the bedroom is overloaded with belongings and begin freeing space. A rule immediately prohibits every extra cushion and throw although these make resting pleasant. **An understood change need not relinquish every familiar support identically.** Discussing actual space and use allows a specific choice. A favourite receives no guarantee of staying but is not declared excessive merely because a new scheme has already been announced as uniquely correct.

The difficulty is answering attachment through an even stricter prohibition. The familiar is defended harder while renewal’s meaning disappears within a struggle over objects. Support grows when both distinguish aim, rule and pleasure. A clear limit can remain discussable: change helps life when its cost is recognised and choice does not become an obligation to prove readiness for novelty by relinquishing every pleasant thing.
